body:
>pyro1488@my-deja.com wrote:

>Is it me or does this sound like 1984?

>Cheers,
>Pyro

It is not just you. Although the media will have you believe it is.
Two stories in a local paper this past weekend had comments regarding
John Rocker's psychological "problems." I will give snippets from each
article. My comments and TK's quotes follow in parentheses.

------------------------------------------
"Yep, John is off his Rocker"
NY Times News Service
By David Grimes

"Like most sensitive Americans, I have spent a great deal of time
wringing my hands over the remarks made by Atlanta Braves pitcher John
Rocker in Sports Illustrated."

(Sensitive is a synonym for leftist)

"The remarks were so offensive that I cannot repeat them here for fear
that you will go blind or your newspaper will spontaneously combust in
your hands."

(An exaggeration with Grimes conveniently omitting the offensive
comments from his article in order to bar the public from judging how
offensive the comments really are. Grimes fits the role of the leftist
as TK stated in paragraph 11 in ISAIF "They [leftists] are
hypersensitive about the words used to designate minorities.  The
terms "negro," "oriental," "handicapped" or "chick" for an African, an
Asian, a disabled person or a woman originally had no derogatory
connotation.  "Broad" and "chick" were merely the feminine equivalents
of "guy," "dude" or "fellow."  The negative connotations have been
 attached to these terms by the activists themselves.")

"Now Rocker is in big trouble. He was made to undergo psychological
testing to see if he has a mental disorder, and there is a possibility
- quite remote, I would think - that he will be kicked off the team
and maybe even banned from baseball."

(I don't believe John Rocker has been MADE to undergo psychological
testing as yet.)

"It is my opinion that Rocker deserves whatever happens to him because
Americans are dependent upon professional athletes for guidance in the
important social issues of our time, and Rocker has let us down."

(Huh? A typical do-gooder leftist statement promoting the "good" of
society over the freedoms of the individual. TK stated in paragraph 16
in ISAIF "The leftist is anti-individualistic, pro-collectivist.  He
wants society to solve everyone's needs for them, take care of them.
He is not the sort of person who has an inner sense of confidence in
his own ability to solve his own problems and satisfy his own needs.
The leftist is antagonistic to the concept of competition because,
deep inside, he feels like a loser.")

____________________
"Some Prespective"
Knight Ridder/Tribune News Service
By Gregory Clay

"Still, Rocker's broad-sweeping, though unspecific, remarks speak for
a vast number of people in this country - from coast to coast. He is
not operating or thinking in a cosmic state of isolationism"

(Again the journalist fails to list specifically John Rocker's
broad-sweeping, though unspecific remarks. And yes, John Rocker is not
thinking in a cosmic state of isolationism and the media and the
"system" are aware of it. And they don't like it. John Rocker MUST not
be loyal to his white European American community for that will make
the system have less power over America's fragmented society.
TK stated in paragraph 51 in ISAIF "In modern society an individual's
loyalty must be first to the system and only secondarily to a
small-scale community, because if the internal loyalties of
small-scale small-scale communities were stronger than loyalty to the
system, such communities would pursue their own advantage at the
expense of the system.")

"The bigger scene involves the Rocker sympathizers. People just like
him who want to maintain that little secret. A secret that permeates
many hidden corridors of this nation. It's not just a baseball secret;
it's a societal one."

(And what "secret" would that be? Other than the subtitle of the
article which stated "Rocker incident reminds us: Racism permeates all
of society," Clay never tells the reader what that little secret is
that the Rocker sympathizers should be so ashamed of. Freedom of
speech? Freedom of thinking differently than what is currently
accepted in society? John Rocker can say whatever he wants as long as
it doesn't interfere with the functioning and molding of America's
multicultural system. TK stated in paragraph 72 in ISAIF "Modern
society is in certain respects extremely permissive. In matters
that are irrelevant to the functioning of the system we can generally
do what we please.  We can believe in any religion we like (as long as
it does not encourage behavior that is dangerous to the system).  We
can go to bed with anyone we like (as long as we practice
"safe sex").  We can do anything we like as long as it is UNIMPORTANT.
But in all IMPORTANT matters the system tends increasingly to regulate
our behavior.")

"So for those who say the Latino, American-born black and
Hispanic-born black players on the team cannot stomach Rocker anymore,
well, just let them settle it with some old-fashioned justice...a
punch or slap directed toward Rocker by those affected and those
offended might solve this internal team problem sooner than you
think."

(Yes physical violence against racists is "good" while supposedly
derogatory words by "racists" against minorities is "bad." All
do-gooders are not as peaceful as they claim to be as TK stated in
ISAIF in paragraph 29 "We certainly do not claim that leftists, even
of the oversocialized type, NEVER rebel against the fundamental values
of our society.  Clearly they sometimes do.  Some oversocialized
leftists have gone so far as to rebel against one of modern
society's most important principles by engaging in physical violence.
By their own account, violence is for them a form of "liberation."  In
other words, by committing violence they break through the
psychological restraints that have been trained into them.  Because
they are oversocialized these restraints have been more confining for
them than for others; hence their need to break free of them.  But
they usually justify their rebellion in terms of mainstream values.
If they engage in violence they claim to be fighting against racism or
the like.")


Now Pug's comments on the psychological testing of John Rocker (which
can also be found in full on alt.misanthropy):

___________________________

Freedom of speech.

I think not.

John Rocker has been ordered by baseball to undergo psychological
tests.

Yes, he is psychologically warped.

Why, you may ask?

Well, John Rocker made some disparaging remarks about gays, minorities
and immigrants in Sports Illustrated last month. John Rocker is white.
Tsk, tsk, zero tolerance John, zero tolerance.

Rocker commented that he would never play for a New York team because
he didn't want to ride a train "next to some queer with AIDS." OK,
sounds logical to me. Hell, I would never live in that shit-hole
called NYC, and it is not just the queers with AIDS that make me leery
of entering that abyss of multiculturalism. Needless to say, John
Rocker won't be getting any fan mail from the gay, oops, homosexual
community.

The paper also said Rocker BASHED immigrants, saying, "I'm not a very
big fan of foreigners...How the hell did they get in this country?" I
am wondering that myself. Of course, America's policy of "wide-open"
doors for immigrants of "color" these past thirty years could account
for it. Needless to say John Rocker won't be getting a call to play
baseball in Cuba or Central America.

John also called a black teammate "a fat monkey." I am sure the black,
oops African American players in baseball have NEVER called their
white teammates anything derogatory, at least not to the media.
Anyway, I suppose it is better than John having called him "a fat
nigger." 

Atlanta Braves president Stan Kasten said of John "But we at least
need to give the man an opportunity to demonstrate his heartfelt
remorse and correct the problem."

What problem? 

Kasten also said of John "He did have a history of good relationships
with players of different races and different ethnic backgrounds."

Again, where is the problem? If John, by his actions had good
relationships with his teammates, even calling them "fat monkeys" why
does the media dwell on his off-the-cuff comments? Is it because
comments about/against minorities are unPC and intolerable in our
multicultural society? Of course in today's society, such comments are
intolerable, even if such comments have some truth to them. John as a
public figure should know his freedom to make comments that do not
agree with the PC media view will not be tolerated. John Rocker has no
freedom to publicly make unpopular comments. He will say what the
media and public wants to hear or he will undergo psychological tests.

Baseball calling for the psychological evaluation of John Rocker is
where I draw the line. Society says John is *evil*, he is *bad* for
using his freedom of speech in our glorious country. He must be
psychologically unstable for EVER making any derogatory comments about
minorities. Of course the media and baseball can make derogatory
comments about John, calling him a racist and psychologically warped,
that is OK.

I am not saing I am the biggest fan of John Rocker, but I am a fan of
freedom of speech, even for public figures. Society is too uptight
about "words" never realizing it is one's actions that prove the
integrity and character of a person. Now, if John were to go out and
start mowing down gays and foreigners with a machine gun, yes I would
agree with society he is psychologically warped and a murderer to
boot. The argument I will get from do-gooders is, "John is a role
model for CHILDREN, and any words he says will be taken literally by
children and they will grow up hating gays, minorities and
foreigners."

Maybe.

But suppressing freedom of speech will not make "hate" and "stupidity"
in our society go away. It'll only make individuals more paranoid,
it'll take away their individuality and yes, make society less
informed and more stupid. 

Rocker later apologized and said he was not a racist, but several
advocacy groups said the written apology was not enough.

Not enough? If I was John Rocker, I would not have apologized. He has
been labeled psychologically unfit to live in today's PC society, he
might as well enjoy the ride.

Pug
(Also labeled psychologically unfit)
